name: MacroGenics, Inc.

profile.description: MacroGenics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes antibody-based therapeutics for cancer treatment. The company's pipeline includes lorigerlimab (bispecific PD-1/CTLA-4), MGC026 (B7-H3 ADC), MGC028 (ADAM9 ADC), and MGC030 (preclinical ADC), with collaborations with Gilead, Incyte, and Sanofi.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): MacroGenics executed a genuine business transformation in 2026 — divesting its GMP drug-substance manufacturing operations to Bora Pharmaceuticals for $122.5M and monetizing ZYNYZ royalties for up to $80M, extending cash runway to 2028 and reshaping the company into a pure R&D-focused biotech [1]. The May 2026 LINNET data cut showed encouraging early efficacy for lorigerlimab in clear cell gynecologic cancer (4 of 16 evaluable patients with objective responses, including one unconfirmed complete response), though no product has reached commercialization [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered drug discovery tools or AI-driven efficiency gains; the company relies on its proprietary DART and antibody engineering platforms without disclosed AI integration [2]. Market Share (1/2): MacroGenics is a meaningful player in the ADC/bispecific space with three clinical-stage ADC candidates (MGC026, MGC028, MGC030) and proprietary linker-payload technology, but does not lead the category against larger competitors like Daiichi Sankyo and AbbVie [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Specific next-gen data readouts are scheduled — MGC026 initial data mid-2026, MGC028 data H2 2026, MGC030 IND filing Q3 2026, and two additional product candidates from proprietary TCE/ADC platforms targeted for nomination by end of 2026 [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D spending remains substantial relative to revenue for this clinical-stage biotech, consistent with industry norms [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): MacroGenics' stated purpose centers on developing differentiated antibody-based therapeutics to improve cancer patient outcomes — clear and relevant but not distinctive among oncology-focused biotechs [3]. Community Impact (1/2): The company contributes to the broader cancer research ecosystem through academic collaborations and partnerships with global pharma companies (Gilead, Incyte, Sanofi), though no specific charitable programs or foundation activities are publicly documented [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor rating of 3.4/5 across 67 reviews with mixed feedback — some praise the culture and people, while others cite micromanagement and burnout from upper management, suggesting average-to-below-average retention [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): CEO Eric Risser (in the role since August 2025, previously COO since 2022, credited with generating over $1.6B in non-dilutive capital since inception) has now executed the Bora manufacturing sale and ZYNYZ royalty monetization, but no meaningful net open-market insider buying data was identified at current depressed prices [2].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on Growth-stock weighting. D/E of 148% scores 0.66 against the 70% target/300% floor. ROE of -87.47% and TTM profit margin of -21.38% both breach their zero floors, scoring 0.0 — the company remains structurally unprofitable as a clinical-stage biotech, though the loss margin has narrowed materially from FY2025's -49.9% following the Bora manufacturing divestiture and royalty monetization [1]. TTM revenue growth of 1.97% scores 0.73. Forward P/E, 5yr revenue CAGR, and PEG are not meaningful/unavailable for this unprofitable name and were excluded from the calculation. Weighted result: 1.39/5.0 weighted units ≈ 3/10. The extended cash runway to 2028 (via the $122.5M Bora sale and up to $80M ZYNYZ royalty monetization) is a credit but is not captured in the mechanical metrics [1]. Liquidity floor passed: 757K avg vol × $4.01 ≈ $3.0M daily turnover [4].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): MacroGenics' core business — wet-lab antibody engineering, clinical trials, and biologic manufacturing — involves physical-world R&D and regulatory processes that AI cannot substitute [1]. Drug development requires FDA clinical trial approval, patient recruitment, and manufacturing scale-up that are inherently human and physical. However, AI-driven drug discovery platforms from competitors (Recursion, Absci, large pharma AI labs) could accelerate competitive pipelines and compress MacroGenics' differentiation in target selection and molecule optimization [2]. The ADC space specifically requires complex bioconjugation chemistry and manufacturing that remains AI-resistant. AI Opportunity (1/1): While MacroGenics has not disclosed AI deployment, the broader pharma industry is using AI for target identification and clinical trial optimization; MacroGenics' collaboration partners Gilead and Incyte are investing in AI tools that could indirectly benefit joint programs [1].

infinite_game.summary: MacroGenics has demonstrated persistence through a 25-year history of antibody platform development, and CEO Eric Risser (in the role since August 2025) has since executed a genuine business-model reshaping — divesting manufacturing and monetizing royalties to extend runway to 2028 while continuing to fund four clinical programs. The collaboration-dependent revenue model and clinical-stage cash burn still create finite-game pressure to deliver near-term pipeline milestones.

just_cause.analysis: MacroGenics was founded in 2000 with a genuine scientific cause — developing next-generation antibody-based cancer therapeutics using proprietary DART and ADC platforms [3]. The cause is specific to oncology and has driven 25 years of consistent platform development, and the May 2026 LINNET data (objective responses including one unconfirmed complete response) offers early validation, but the cause has not yet been proven by a commercial product. Just Cause: 1 point.

trusting_teams.analysis: Mixed signals — Glassdoor reviews (3.4/5) show some employees value the culture and collaborative environment, but others cite micromanagement and burnout driven by upper management [2]. The 2025 CEO transition to Risser and the 2026 divestiture of the manufacturing unit (moving ~140 employees to Bora) create organizational change, though Risser's internal promotion from COO provided continuity. Trusting Teams: 1 point.

worthy_rivals.analysis: MacroGenics operates in a competitive ADC landscape against Daiichi Sankyo (Enhertu), AbbVie, and Pfizer/Seagen, but there is no public evidence of management framing these as worthy rivals whose strengths drive MacroGenics' improvement [1]. The competitive language is typical biotech — focused on differentiated targets and novel payloads rather than learning from rivals. Worthy Rivals: 0 points.

existential_flexibility.analysis: MacroGenics executed a genuine reinvention in 2026 — selling its GMP drug-substance manufacturing operations to Bora Pharmaceuticals for $122.5M and monetizing ZYNYZ royalties for up to $80M, transforming from a partly vertically-integrated manufacturer into a pure R&D-focused biotech and extending cash runway to 2028 [1]. This followed the earlier evolution from its original DART bispecific focus into a three-candidate ADC pipeline (MGC026, MGC028, MGC030). Existential Flexibility: 2 points.

courage_to_lead.analysis: CEO Eric Risser has made multiple consequential capital-allocation bets in 2026: divesting the manufacturing business, monetizing future royalties, and continuing to fund four clinical programs (MGC026, MGC028, MGC030, lorigerlimab) simultaneously despite a depressed ~$255M market cap [1][2]. This is a pattern of costly, long-term-oriented decisions rather than a single bet. Courage to Lead: 2 points.

investment_thesis: MacroGenics has re-rated modestly to a ~$255M market cap after executing a business transformation in 2026: selling its GMP manufacturing operations to Bora Pharmaceuticals for $122.5M upfront and monetizing ZYNYZ royalties for up to $80M, extending cash runway to 2028 without new equity dilution [1]. Q1 2026 revenue rose to $20.8M from $13.2M YoY and the net loss narrowed to $36.8M from $41.0M [1]. The May 2026 LINNET data cut showed encouraging early signal for lorigerlimab in clear cell gynecologic cancer (4 of 16 evaluable patients with objective responses, including one unconfirmed complete response), and MGC026/MGC028 Phase 1 data plus an MGC030 IND filing are all still on deck for 2026 [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case remains substantial: MacroGenics has been public since 2013 without a commercial product, and TTM profit margin is still deeply negative at -21.38% with ROE of -87.47% [3][4]. The Bora/ZYNYZ deals buy time (runway to 2028) rather than resolve the core question of whether any pipeline asset reaches approval. The lorigerlimab CCGC signal is real but early — MacroGenics is now enrolling an additional 20 patients at a lower dose specifically to improve the safety/efficacy balance, meaning the readout is not yet definitive. The ADC competitive landscape remains intense with well-funded programs from Daiichi Sankyo, AbbVie, and others, and any negative Phase 1 data on MGC026 or MGC028 later in 2026 could trigger renewed equity dilution risk despite the extended runway.
key_catalysts: MGC026 (B7-H3 ADC) initial Phase 1 data expected mid-2026, targeting a validated oncology antigen with a novel TOP1i linker-payload [1]
Lorigerlimab LINNET expansion cohort (20 additional CCGC patients at a lower 3 mg/kg dose) reading out following the encouraging May 2026 data cut (25% ORR, one unconfirmed CR) [1]
MGC030 IND submission planned Q3 2026 plus nomination of two additional product candidates from proprietary TCE/ADC platforms by year-end 2026 [1]
key_risks: Negative Phase 1 data for MGC026 or MGC028 would undermine the ADC platform thesis and could trigger renewed equity dilution despite the extended cash runway [1]
The company remains structurally unprofitable (TTM profit margin -21.38%, ROE -87.47%) and dependent on lumpy collaboration/milestone revenue [3][4]
The lorigerlimab CCGC signal is based on a small, uncontrolled cohort (16 evaluable patients) and the dose is being lowered for the expansion cohort, meaning efficacy is not yet confirmed [1]
